key_insight: Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators replace flow-based constraints with autoregressive modeling to generate equilibrium molecular samples more expressively and efficiently.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable path to faster, transferable molecular sampling for computational chemistry and protein design, especially for larger peptide systems.
method: Uses an autoregressive generative framework instead of normalizing flows
Supports sequential inference-time interventions and avoids strict invertibility/topology limits
Introduces Robin, a 132M-parameter transferable model trained with ArBG
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved performance across benchmarks, with especially strong gains on larger peptide systems and over 60% reduction in zero-shot energy error on 8-residue systems.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-driven, so practical gains may depend on system size, training data coverage, and whether the autoregressive model remains efficient for more complex molecular topologies.
